records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale eagerly on every fallback lookup, so any I18n translate with fallbacks triggered before the database is connected (boot-time initializers, assets:precompile on a machine without the DB, early rake tasks) executes a SiteSetting read against a missing connection. Operators running `rake assets:precompile` or bootstrap tasks on a fresh checkout without a migrated DB get an uninitialized-constant/connection error from a config-time lookup that previously (config.i18n.fallbacks = true) never touched SiteSetting.

records.issue_text: [BUG] FallbackLocaleList overrides Hash#[] to always compute a fresh array, so any external write to the fallbacks map becomes a silent no-op. Code that configures fallbacks via the standard I18n API (e.g. `I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de, :en]` from a plugin, admin setting, or spec setup) stores the entry via []=, but the overridden [] never reads stored values — every subsequent lookup silently ignores the configured fallback chain and returns the hard-coded [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] instead.
records.rationale: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `def [](locale)` to always return a freshly computed array `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` and never calls `super` or consults stored hash entries. Since `[]=` is not overridden, external code can still do `I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [...]` and it will be stored in the underlying Hash, but any later read via `I18n.fallbacks[:de]` will ignore that stored value and return the hard-coded chain. This matches the finding’s described silent no-op for configured fallbacks via the standard API.

records.issue_text: [BUG] ensure_loaded! is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale, so fallback locales are never loaded on any non-request path (background jobs, Sidekiq mailers, scheduled tasks, console-rendered emails). With config.i18n.fallbacks removed from production.rb and replaced by FallbackLocaleList, a Sidekiq job rendering a localized email for locale :fr falls back to :en, but the TranslateAccelerator backend has only loaded :fr (translate calls load_locale(config.locale) alone), so the :en fallback lookup misses and the email ships raw translation keys / missing-translation spans; the fallback feature silently works only for web requests.
